properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 9 at 1:02AM CDT until October 9 at 1:45AM CDT by NWS Sioux Falls SD
properties.description:
SVRFSD

The National Weather Service in Sioux Falls has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Central Cherokee County in northwestern Iowa...
East Central Plymouth County in northwestern Iowa...

* Until 145 AM CDT.

* At 102 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Marcus, or 15
miles west of Cherokee, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Golf ball size hail.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect damage
to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Marcus around 110 AM CDT.
Cleghorn around 120 AM CDT.
Cherokee around 135 AM CDT.

Other locations impacted by the severe thunderstorm include Meriden
and Larrabee.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. This storm has produced dangerous hail.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Sioux Falls SD.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 9 at 1:00AM CDT until October 10 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
...POTENTIAL FOR LIFE THREATENTING FLASH FLOODING...

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Alabama, including the following areas, Baldwin
Central, Baldwin Coastal, Baldwin Inland, Butler, Choctaw, Clarke,
Conecuh, Covington, Crenshaw, Escambia, Mobile Central, Mobile
Coastal, Mobile Inland, Monroe, Washington and Wilcox and northwest
Florida, including the following areas, Escambia Coastal, Escambia
Inland, Okaloosa Coastal, Okaloosa Inland, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Santa Rosa Inland.

* WHEN...From this afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Hurricane Isaias will move onshore on the northern Gulf coast
Friday evening, with bands of rain ahead of the storm moving
onshore Friday afternoon. From Friday through the early Saturday,
Isaias is expected to produce rainfall amounts of 4 to 8 inches
across the region. Localized totals of 10 to 15 inches are
possible, particularly within banding across the Florida
Panhandle and close to the center track of the storm. Flash and
urban flooding is likely across the region, with considerable
impacts possible across much of southern Alabama and the Florida
Panhandle. River flooding is also expected, some of which could
be significant.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay weather aware and be ready to take action if Flash Flood
Warnings are issued, particularly wireless emergency alert Flash
Flood Warnings for considerable flooding.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 8 at 6:11PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by around Tuesday of next week. This
trough is likely to remain strong and active through the duration
of next week, and may even intensify with embedded low pressure
centers. Widespread showers may be heavy and persistent at times
with the possibility of thunderstorms Tuesday through the weekend.
Widespread flash flooding may occur from this rainfall.
Landslides will be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
While there is still uncertainty in the exact magnitude and
duration of rainfall, plan now for wet conditions next Tuesday
through Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 8 at 11:57PM CDT until October 9 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL
AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY...

.Breezy and dry conditions on the outer periphery of Hurricane
Isaias combined with dry fuels will produce red flag conditions
across portions of central and southwest Louisiana and southeast
Texas Friday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 031 Allen, Fire
Weather Zone 032 Evangeline, Fire Weather Zone 259 Northern
Jasper, Fire Weather Zone 260 Northern Newton, Fire Weather
Zone 261 Southern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 262 Southern
Newton.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 7 PM CDT Friday.

* WINDS...Northeast 5 to 10 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 31 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 91.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 8 at 9:45PM PDT until October 14 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.4 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 11:22 AM
Friday 10/9, 1.4 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:50 AM
Saturday 10/10, 1.3 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:18 PM
Sunday 10/11, 1.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:46 PM
Monday 10/12, 1.1 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 1:46 PM
Wednesday 10/14. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
